object_description: four staggered prismatic volumes around a central courtyard
design_condition: The volumes are arranged around a central courtyard and placed toward one side of the site to preserve mature trees, create a park-like perimeter, and connect the campus naturally to the surrounding district.

positive.statement: The carefully proportioned courtyard figure integrates the denser campus well into the garden-city context.

position.rationale: The central courtyard void is clearly enclosed by staggered prismatic volumes.

positive.statement: The arrangement preserves many large-crowned trees and creates varied, connected outdoor spaces.

position.target: large-crowned trees and connected outdoor spaces
position.rationale: Preserved landscape is assigned around the less occupied perimeter beyond the courtyard volumes.

positive.statement: Giving each school level its own building strengthens address and makes orientation easier.

position.rationale: Separate wings are visibly distributed around the courtyard, supporting distinct addresses.

positive.statement: The school wings provide a solid and flexible spatial structure for contemporary teaching and learning.

position.rationale: The four visible wings form a solid, adaptable spatial framework.

positive.statement: The schoolyard and community centre offer welcome public added value and a point of identification.

position.rationale: Public value is anchored in the open ground areas adjoining the courtyard-forming buildings.

positive.statement: Good space efficiency, compactness, timber construction and large photovoltaic areas promise a favourable cost and CO2 balance.

position.rationale: Efficiency and material-performance judgment is associated with the compact visible building ensemble.

negative.statement: The enclosure of the anterooms may fragment the open space and reduce its generosity.

position.rationale: Enclosure criticism is located along the courtyard’s interior edge.

negative.statement: The proximity of the volumes to the neighbouring path reduces the quality of the vegetative border.

position.rationale: The affected landscape edge is approximated along the building perimeter.

negative.statement: A direct line of sight to the community-centre entrance from the street is desirable.

position.rationale: Street-facing entrance visibility is approximated at the south edge of the complex.

negative.statement: The community centre’s mix of uses does not yet provide sufficient operational synergies.

position.rationale: Operational concerns are assigned to one peripheral wing presumed to contain the community centre.

negative.statement: The SKB access organization does not match the qualities of the other school wings.

position.rationale: Access criticism is placed at a distinct outer school wing.

negative.statement: The school’s architectural expression remains schematic and uniform, giving it a somewhat temporary feel.

position.rationale: Uniform expression is anchored to the visible south-facing facade sequence.

negative.statement: The revised north-facing catering rooms may have seriously limited quality of stay because of insufficient sunlight.

position.rationale: North orientation constrains the rooms to the rear edge of the building ensemble.

negative.statement: The roof structure makes the community building appear less open than previously indicated.

position.rationale: Roof criticism is assigned to the upper surface of the presumed community wing.

negative.statement: The large footprint creates cramped ground-level open spaces, particularly around the running track.

position.target: ground-level open spaces around running track
position.rationale: Cramped openness is located across the low ground plane near the presumed track edge.

negative.statement: The urban-planning approach severely impairs the surrounding green space and reduces its generosity and depth.

position.rationale: Urban-planning criticism is assigned to the preserved but narrowed peripheral green area.
